However, the comment only mentions the method itself as a content topic and does not explicitly identify where in the paper this is addressed, such as a specific section, paragraph, table, or figure. According to the rubric's grounding dimension, a comment must explicitly mention which part of the paper it addresses, or it should be obvious to the authors, in order to reach the higher grounding threshold; merely naming the mitigating method does not satisfy that requirement. On the specificity side, the comment does clearly specify what needs to be addressed: an analysis of how and why pretraining on CANDLE contributed to geo-diverse commonsense inference. Thus, while the comment meets the specificity requirement, its grounding is weaker because the authors cannot confidently pinpoint the referenced part of the paper.
